paper_title: Small Learned Projections for Semantic-Reversal-Aware Retrieval with Spectral Acceleration: A Four-Domain Empirical Study

sections.title: Abstract
sections.content: Dense-embedding retrievers can fail adversarially: when a query is answered by a document A and reversed by a near-copy B that differs from A by a small meaning-changing edit (a "trap"), raw cosine over E5-Large-v2 places B in the top-10 for 82-100% of queries at a pool of 5,000. We study two things. First, a small learned projection W: R^1024 -> R^d (d in {11, 32}), trained by a deterministic recipe on a declared set of cases, that suppresses the trap: for the declared cases, HN@10 = 0.0000 (no trap in the top-10) in all twelve (domain, pool-size) settings across four independent domains (legal, medical, patent, financial) and pools up to 100,000, while the correct paraphrase is retained for 93-99% of cases, under exact nearest-neighbour search. Second, a boundary-conditioned accelerator that serves the projection at that scale: an acceleration of spectral graph retrieval (SpectRAG) that replaces a dense eigendecomposition with a boundary-value solve, holding HN@10 = 0.0000 at n = 100,000 in every domain and retrieving the ~300-query suite in 0.6-1.1 s (~2-4 ms per query on average). Because the lens's output is the stored representation (a few floats per document), a hardened, specialised index per domain or tenant is ~90x smaller and dimension-proportionally faster than the full embedding, making many small declared indexes a practical alternative to one large vector store. The claim is scoped to the declared cases on the measured pools, with no probabilistic bound; the correct-answer rate drops for a reworded query against an unchanged corpus (about 0.79, trap suppression still holding). A projection transfers only partly to other domains, which we report in full. The recipe, lenses, trap sets and evaluation harness are released under AGPL-3.0; the accelerator's implementation is a reserved commercial component, and every HN number is reproducible under exact search.

sections.title: 1 Introduction
sections.content: Adversarial trap corpora are the strongest available stress-test for dense-embedding retriever. Unlike random-negative distractorswhich are trivially rejecteda trap document differs from the correct answer by small meaning-changing editoften single token (must vs. must not, 500 mg vs. 5000 mg, comprising vs. consisting 1 Small Learned Projections Reduce Semantic-Reversal Errors in Dense Retrieval 2 of, increased vs. decreased), and short multi-token edit in the legal corpus. Cosine similarity in the embedding space assigns near-identical scores to and B, so routinely appears in the top-k retrieved list for any query anchored on A. In domains with regulatory or compliance stakes (legal contracts, medical treatment guidelines, patent claim scope, financial disclosures), trap surfacing in top-10 is silent operational failurethe retriever confidently returns document that reverses the intended semantics of the query. The dense retriever we measure (raw cosine over E5-Large-v2, no task prefixes) is trap-vulnerable in this configuration: without lens, the trap reaches the top-10 for 82100 % of queries at pool of 5 000 documents (6). Whether other encoders and configurations behave the same is not measured here (7.2). Our contribution is training procedure that produces small linear projection which keeps the trap out of the top-10 for the cases it is declared for, without collapsing retrieval utility (3.1). The mechanism is not novel in isolation. Learned linear projections trained with preservation loss plus hard-negative hinge term are standard building blocks in the metric-learning literature. What we contribute is: 1. precise construction recipe that gives zero trap hits for the declared cases in every domain we measured, with the same code path. 2. Four-domain empirical validationlegal, medical, patent, financialwith matched methodology and zero per-domain code changes. 3. cross-domain transfer experiment. Every trained lens is applied to the other domains trap corpora. lens is built for its own domains cases; the experiment marks where it applies. Poor transfer is the expected outcome, but good transfer would not refute the recipe: lens could also learn structure the domains share. 4. complete 44 transfer matrix measuring twelve mismatched-lens/trap-corpus pairs. Eleven stay at HN@10 [0.44, 0.85]; one sits at HN@10 = 0.2957, below the 0.30 the pre-registration had set, and is reported as missed. 5. Reproducibility infrastructure. SHA-256-anchored artefacts, deterministic trapgeneration scripts, preflight duplicate-check guardrail, and an OSS release under AGPL-3.0. We report enough measurement detail that any reader with modest CPU-only machine and 24 GB of RAM can reproduce every number in the paper within working day. Summary of contributions 6-step recipe (3) HN@10 = 0.0000 on four domains; complete 4 4 transfer matrix (6.3): 11 of 12 off-diagonal cells at HN@10 [0.44, 0.85]; the 12th (Legal = 11 on Patent, HN@10 = 0.2957) is below the pre-registered 0.30 and reported as missed; = 32 retrain (6.4) explains it but does not pass it. The trap sets, generators, lenses, trainer and harness are released as pelloran-safety-lens under AGPL-3.0. Small Learned Projections Reduce Semantic-Reversal Errors in Dense Retrieval

sections.title: 2 Related Work
sections.content: Dense retrieval baselines. E5-Large-v2 (Wang et al., 2023), BGE-Large (Chen et al., 2024), and GTE-Large (Li et al., 2023) are representative of the 1024-dimensional sentence-encoder class, producing L2-normalisable dense embeddings with cosine as the natural similarity. In this paper we measure only E5-Large-v2 on the four trap corpora; the underlying embedding geometry that produces the trap vulnerability is shared across the class (both and lie inside the same near-token-copy neighbourhood in cosine space), so the same behaviour on BGE / GTE is hypothesis for further experiments; we have not measured it (see Limitations, 7.2). Hybrid densesparse retrieval. BM25/dense hybrids (Robertson and Zaragoza, 2009; Karpukhin et al., 2020) and ColBERT-style late-interaction models (Khattab and Zaharia, 2020) are not, in general, defence against the specific trap class studied here: our differs from by single semantically-reversing token (must vs. must not), so BM25 assigns and near-identical lexical scores and hybrid densesparse retrievers inherit the dense components trap-fall. We report Cell (raw cosine) as the dense-only baseline and do not run BM25 experiment because we do not expect it to move on this trap taxonomy; hybrid comparison on trap classes with wider lexical spread is scoped for follow-up work, not claimed here. Adversarial IR. The adversarial-retrieval literature is dominated by black-box attack generation on the offensive side (Guo et al., 2019; Song et al., 2020; Wu et al., 2022). Our work sits on the defense side: given known trap taxonomy, how to train projection that suppresses trap-fall while preserving utility. Negation in neural retrieval (NevIR). Weller et al. (2024) build benchmark of document pairs that differ only by negation and ask retrieval models to rank each pair for query. Most models rank at or below chance; cross-encoders do best, then lateinteraction models, with bi-encoders and sparse models last; fine-tuning on contrastive negation data helps but leaves large gap. Our trap pairs are of the same kindone meaning-reversing differencebut cover more contrasts than negation (quantities, claim scope, direction), and our remedy is small projection on top of frozen biencoder rather than different retriever architecture. We do not evaluate on NevIR here (7.2). Metric learning and steering vectors. Preservation-plus-hinge losses are standard in metric learning (Xing et al., 2003; Schroff et al., 2015; Sohn, 2016). Steering vectors for language models (Turner et al., 2023; Zou et al., 2023) apply similar structural interventions on model activations. Our lens is closest to supervised linear steering projection trained on small A/B/C triple set with the hinge term operating in the projected space. Spectral graph retrieval (SpectRAG). Sahinoglu et al. (2026) propose SpectRAG, spectral graph-augmented retriever for multi-hop retrieval-augmented generation. It builds weighted graph over document chunks whose edges encode semantic similarity, document adjacency, section hierarchy, shared entities, citation links, and similarity Small Learned Projections Reduce Semantic-Reversal Errors in Dense Retrieval 4 between LLM-generated utility questions, and it selects the final context under fixed token budget. We build directly on this formulation. The serving layer of our pipeline (3.9) is an acceleration of SpectRAGthe same spectral-retrieval formulation, with the dense eigendecomposition replaced by boundary-conditioned equilibrium solve which lifts it from few thousand chunks to the 105-document pools used here. We do not re-run the original dense SpectRAG at these scales (it does not reach them); we cite it as the method we extend. Duplicate contamination as rigour gate. Benchmark inflation from duplicate nearcopies is well-documented failure mode in NLP evaluation (Dodge et al., 2021; Lee et al., 2022). Our data-quality audit (3.5) surfaces 22 % duplicate rate in an early version of our legal trap corpus that inflated HitC@10 by 16 pp. We ship the resulting preflight guardrail as hard gate before any lens training run.

sections.title: 3.1 What a lens is declared for
sections.content: A case is one specific contrasting statement pair: statement A, its trap (A with one meaning-reversing change), and paraphrase of A. For example, Metformin is dosed at 500 mg twice daily for adults with type-2 diabetes, the same sentence with 5000 mg, and Adults with type-2 diabetes receive metformin 500 mg BID. case is not contrast type: dosage flips in general is type; the metformin pair is case. lens is declared for set of casesan insurers contract terms AA, BB and CC, sayand is trained on exactly those. For declared case it is meant to keep out of the top-10 for query anchored on A, and in it, in the evaluated distractor pools. Cases outside the declared setincluding new statement pairs of the same typeare not covered by design: one declares and trains lens for them (DD, EE), combines lenses, or declares the whole set (AA to EE) from the start. trap is unwanted where the reader needs the statement as it stands: answering, compliance and clause retrieval, where returning must not for must reverses the answer. Where the contradiction itself is soughta search for conflicting clauses or for change between versionsB is relevant result, and no lens is applied. Figure 1 summarises the six deterministic steps of the recipe. Every step is described in detail in the subsections that follow.

sections.title: 3.3 Distractor pool
sections.content: For each domain we assemble distractor pool of 50 000 short (830 word) clauses in the target domain, sentence-split from public corpus. Matched-shape distractors are essential mixing sentence-length A/B/C with paragraph-length distractors makes the retrieval geometry noise-dominated (Appendix B, failure mode 3). Sources per domain: Legal: LexGLUE, sentence-split. Medical: PubMed abstracts, sentence-split, 200 000 unique. Patent: HuggingFace BIGPATENT abstracts, sentence-split across eight USPTO categories, 182 335 unique. Financial: five HuggingFace financial NLP datasets combined and sentence-split, 177 561 unique.

sections.title: 3.4 Embedding
sections.content: We use intfloat/e5-large-v2 (Wang et al., 2023). No task prefix (passage: / query:) applied. L2-normalisation after encoding. 1024-dimensional output. The training procedure is architecture-agnostic; the choice of E5 here is representative rather than load-bearing. Small Learned Projections Reduce Semantic-Reversal Errors in Dense Retrieval

sections.title: 3.5 Preflight duplicate-check guardrail
sections.content: Before training, we compute SHA-256 hashes of every triples flattened f32 embedding bytes and refuse to proceed if 5 % of case rows are byte-identical duplicates. This is hard gate. In an early experiment on the legal corpus we discovered 22 % duplicate rate that had silently inflated HitC@10 by 16 percentage points; the guardrail enforces the discipline at generation time. Preflight-check code and threshold rationale ship in the OSS release.

sections.title: 3.6 Lens training
sections.content: The lens is matrix R1024d with {11, 24, 32}. Training minimises: L(W ) = α Lpreserve(W ) + β Lhinge(W ) + λ mean(W 2) where: Lpreserve(W ) is the mean-squared error between the preand post-projection pairwise cosine similarities, over sampled batch of distinct document pairs (all < j, not only positive pairs). It preserves the geometry that makes retrieval work. Lhinge(W ) is the per-triple max(cid:0)0, cos(Aproj, Bproj)cos(Aproj, Cproj)+margin(cid:1). It pushes the trap away from the query in the projected space while keeping the utility target close. α = 1.0, β {10, 15, 17}, margin {0.05, 0.10, 0.12}, λ = 1104. The regulariser is the mean of the squared entries of , not summed norm, so λ is scaled to that convention. Optimiser: Adam, learning rate 5 103, pairs_per_epoch = 8000, epochs = 200, seed = 42 (fully deterministic). Warm-starting from prior lens (init-aqwt) shortens convergence and closes the last percentage points of hn_loss. For new domain from cold-start, = 32 and β = 15 typically produces near-zero hn_loss; second warm-start round with the same configuration or β = 17 eliminates the residual. β = 20 destabilises training (see Appendix C). Training wall-clock: approximately 90 per lens on modern multi-core CPU (an AMD EPYC server, no GPU). No gradient checkpointing or mixed precision required.

sections.title: 3.7 Cross-domain transfer experiment
sections.content: The final step of the recipe. Take the freshly trained domain-X lens and measure it on the trap corpora of the other domains. lens is built for its own domains cases, so we expect it to do much worse there; the experiment shows where lens applies. It is not validity test: lens that also separated another domains traps would have learned structure the domains share, not failed. Our pre-registration had set HN@10 0.30 off-domain as criterion. We report that criterion as it was written (6.3), but no longer treat it as condition for the recipes validity.

sections.title: 3.8 Determinism and reproducibility infrastructure
sections.content: Every step of the recipe is deterministic given fixed seed and pinned dependencies: Small Learned Projections Reduce Semantic-Reversal Errors in Dense Retrieval 8 Trap generators emit the identical 301-triple corpus for given seed = 42. E5 embedding is deterministic in fp32. Preflight duplicate check is pure hash operation. Adam with fixed seed is deterministic in CPU-only mode. The measurement harness reports raw counts, not probabilistic estimates. Every artefact (trap corpus, distractor pool, lens weight matrix, measurement JSON) is anchored by SHA-256 in Appendix A. Re-running the pipeline with the same seed and pinned dependencies reproduces the SHA exactly.

sections.title: 3.9 Serving at scale: a boundary-conditioned spectral retrieval accelerator
sections.content: The lens is reranking primitive. To serve it over pools of 105 documents we pair it with spectral retrieval accelerator. SpectRAG (Sahinoglu et al., 2026) selects context by spectral analysis of similarity graph over document chunks. Building that spectral structure densely requires an eigendecomposition of the graph Laplacian an offline, per-corpus cost of O(n3) that, in our measurements, exhausts memory well before = 100 000 and so caps the corpus size dense build can index. Our accelerator keeps the spectral-retrieval formulation but avoids the dense eigendecomposition. Writing the graph Laplacian in block form with small boundary set (the query-anchored seeds) and interior I, the equilibrium field over the interior is the discrete harmonic extension eq = L1 II LIB TB LII = LIB TB, the Dirichlet solution (Schur complement) of the boundary conditions. The interior field eq scores the interior nodes and the retrieval ranking is read off from it, so one boundary-value solve replaces the per-query spectral scoring. Fixed boundary, varying values. The boundary set is fixed at the corpus level (a small set of anchor vertices); query sets only the boundary values TBits similarities to the boundary documentschanging the right-hand side LIB TB but not LII . The factorisation of LII is therefore computed once per corpus and reused by every query, which is solve against that fixed factorisation. Three costs separate: Graph build assembling the sparse Laplacian over the pool: offline, per corpus. Factorisation of LII offline, per corpus, amortised over all queries. Per-query solve the boundary setup and the triangular or iterative solves that produce eq . conditional complexity claim. We do not claim near-linearity unconditionally. If LII is banded with bandwidth bounded independently of n, banded Cholesky factorisation and each triangular solve are O(n b2)linear in for fixed b; equivalently, an unfactorised Krylov solve costs O(n m) for sparsity and iteration count m, nearlinear when and stay bounded on the retrieval graph (with preconditioning where Small Learned Projections Reduce Semantic-Reversal Errors in Dense Retrieval 9 needed). Our engines construction keeps the interior Laplacian in this boundedbandwidth regime; that construction is the proprietary part and is not disclosed. The claim is therefore conditional on the stated bounded-bandwidth (resp. boundediteration) assumptionnot theorem about arbitrary retrieval graphs; the measured wall-clock is in 6.2. The accelerator is an optional, swappable backend. The lens emits L2-normalised d-dimensional vectors; of the two backends we measure the accelerator and the exact-nearest-neighbour substitute shipped in pelloran-safety-lensboth return the same HN@10 on these pools. (A projection does not by itself guarantee that an arbitrary downstream retriever selects the same documents; we claim this only for the two backends we compared.) The accelerator supplies the latency and the 100 000-document reach (Cell D, 6.2); the safety property does not depend on it.

sections.title: 4 Cell-based Measurement Framework
sections.content: We measure retrieval quality with four cells per pool-size configuration: Cell raw E5 cosine, no lens, no graph. The baseline every dense-retrieval system starts from. Cell 3-stage cascade: utility projection (Wu) top-k lens top-10. Pure projections, no graph. Cell lens projection with exact nearest-neighbour search over the projected pool. This is the open, reproducible safety measurement: every HN@10 number in 6 is from this cell, and it reproduces in pelloran-safety-lens. Cell the same lens served by the spectral accelerator of 3.9 (the deployed pipeline). HN@10 is identical to Cell C; Cell adds the 0.61.1 suite retrieval (24 ms per query) and the 100 000-document reach of 6.2. Its numbers are measured and SHA-anchored; its retriever is reserved commercial component. For each cell we report: HN@10 hard-negative rate at = 10, defined as the fraction of queries where the trap appears in the top-10 retrieved documents. HitC@10 correct-answer rate at = 10, defined as the fraction of queries where the paraphrase appears in the top-10. Cell is the deployed pipeline; Cell is its open, exact-search reproduction, with identical HN@10. The domain-agnostic claim is carried by Cells and together. Cells and are reference points. Scope note. The spectral accelerator underlying Cell is out-of-scope for this paper; only its interface is documented (the mathematics of why it is near-linear is given in 3.9). The lens produced by the recipe in 3 operates independently of this retriever and can be paired with any retrieval backend that consumes L2-normalised d-dimensional embeddings. Readers reproducing the paper use the exact-nearestneighbour backend on the projected pool (Cell C): every HN@10 number in 6 is Small Learned Projections Reduce Semantic-Reversal Errors in Dense Retrieval 10 measured that way, with the packages exact search. The accelerators latency (Cell D) requires the commercial retriever or an equivalent near-linear spectral backend. Figure 2 contrasts the cells by the operations each applies between the shared E5Large-v2 embedding of the query and the returned top-10 documents. The measurement cells. All share the same E5-Large-v2 embedding of the query and differ in the operations applied to the pool before the top-10 is returned. Cell is the dense-retrieval baseline; Cell is the lens-only 3-stage cascade; the lens column feeds two interchangeable backendsCell (exact nearest-neighbour, open and reproducible) and Cell (the spectral accelerator, reserved commercial; dashed box)which return the same HN@10 (see 4 scope note).

sections.title: 6.7 Robustness to rewording (Legal)
sections.content: The declared cases can be stated in words the lens was not trained on. We rewrite the declared Legal cases with fixed, fully-listed carrier lexicon under per-case check that keeps each cases trap-discriminating tokens byte-identical, so the one-token trap edit is preserved by construction; the check proves preserved token differences, not full semantic equivalence. Two tests measure different things. Joint rewording (query and corpus together). Applying the lexicon identically to A, and rewrites the query and the stored documents consistently; 194 of the 299 cases admit such safe rewrite. The rewordings are faithful (mean E5 cosine to the source 0.99) but deliberately mild the safe lexicon never touches discriminator, so this is lower bound on the stress. Here the shipped lens holds HitC@10 = 0.9845 and HN@10 = 0.0155 (3 of 194 cases), against 0.0052 (1 of 194) on the trained phrasings; without the lens the trap reaches the top-10 for about 81 % of these cases. Declaring the phrasings closes the residual: an improved lens fine-tuned from the shipped one on the declared cases plus one reworded variant reaches HN@10 = 0.0000 on the declared phrasings and 0.0103 on second, held-out variant (vs. 0.0258 for the shipped lens), at about one point of HitC@10 on the originals the concept-scoped method by design, not post-hoc fit to the evaluation. Query-only rewording (the practical case). Here the query vector is the reworded but the search pool is the unchanged original corpus the original A, B, and distractors, with no reworded row in it (the cases own original is still excluded from its ranking). This asks whether differently-worded user query still finds the right passage in an unchanged corpus. The safety property holds HN@10 = 0.0052 (1 of 194) but utility drops: HitC@10 = 0.7938 for the shipped lens, down from 0.9845 under joint rewording, because the reworded query matches the original paraphrase less well. The improved lens scores 0.8763 on these same queries, but this phrasing (v1) is in its training set, so that figure is fit to declared wordings, not generalization: on phrasing it was not trained on (v2), the two lenses are comparable shipped 0.8093, improved 0.7784 i.e. declaring and fitting helps the declared wordings, not arbitrary Small Learned Projections Reduce Semantic-Reversal Errors in Dense Retrieval 19 unseen queries. So the lenss trap suppression is robust to query rewording, but its retrieval utility on reworded queries is markedly lower (0.780.81) and does not improve for undeclared phrasings. These absolute counts are small and the observation is correspondingly limited.

sections.title: 7.1 Interpretation of the results
sections.content: Shared structure, partial transfer. The 4 4 matrix (6.3) does not show purely domain-specific lens. Every foreign lens lowers HN@10 below raw cosine the Legal lens takes Patent from 0.9967 to 0.2957so the lenses carry some structure the domains share. None reaches the declared-case 0.0000 off-domain: full suppression holds for the declared cases only. Its per-corpus artefact. Four independent corpora, four independent trap taxonomies, four independent distractor sourcessame result. Reproducing this on fifth independent domain (bioinformatics, semiconductor process, insurancepolicy, or scientific-claim traps) with the same recipe would push the not artefact claim past reasonable doubt; this is our next experimental milestone.

sections.title: 7.2 What the evidence does not establish
sections.content: Limitations at glance 1. Constructed traps. The 299301 test cases per domain are hand-authored matched-shape trapssingle-token in three domains, short edits in legal. This is deliberate stress test, not natural-language corpus. Transfer to naturally-occurring adversarial examples (multi-token flips, long-form contradictions) is not established here. 2. Single encoder tested. All reported numbers use E5-Large-v2. The training procedure is architecture-agnostic in principle; behaviour on BGE-Large / GTE-Large is hypothesis for further experiments, not measured. 3. Outside the declared set, by design. Cases outside lenss declared set including new statement pairs of the same typeare not covered (3.1); one declares and trains lens for them, or combines lenses. 4. No full transfer to new domain. foreign lens lowers HN@10 but does not reach 0.0000 (6.3); new domains cases need their own lens, trained on 300 in-domain triples. 5. Cell latency is proprietary. The 0.61.1 suite retrieval (Cell D; 24 ms per query) relies on our commercial spectral accelerator (3.9); its numbers are measured and SHA-anchored, but the implementation is not released. The open-source exact-nearest-neighbour substitute (Cell C) reproduces every HN@10 number; its time per query was not measured here. 6. Other components out of scope. proprietary enterprise retriever and additional re-ranking and fusion components are out of scope and not part of this release; Cell Bs retrieval quality is tabulated only on Legal, in the same-pool comparison  (Table 3)  ; the other domains cascade quality is not, to keep the claim isolated to the lens projection. Small Learned Projections Reduce Semantic-Reversal Errors in Dense Retrieval 20 7. No E5 task prefixes. We embed without the query: / passage: prefixes that the E5 model card recommends; results with the recommended prefixes are not measured. 8. Some baselines still open. The projection without its preservation or hinge term, cross-encoder reranker, an evaluation on NevIR (Weller et al., 2024), and several seeds for the = 32 follow-up are not part of this paper. Random projection and PCA at the same (6.6) and the cascade-versusaccelerator timing on the same pool (6.2) are now measured. 9. Determinism in the tested environment. The bit-identical re-runs hold for the pinned dependencies on the CPUs we tested; other hardware or library versions may differ in the last digits of float. The Limitations box above lists the points critical reader should flag; few of them warrant longer discussion. Constructedness is intentional. The 299301 test cases per domain are hand-authored matched-shape traps (single-token in three domains, short multi-token edits in legal) adversarial constructions, not sampled from natural distribution of retrieval failures. This is deliberate: the papers claim is that specific stress-test class (small meaning-reversing edits inside short clauses of the target-domain vocabulary) is fully suppressible with small learned projection. Natural-language adversarial transfer (multi-token flips, long-form contradictions, real user queries that misfire) is separate empirical question and is future work. We prefer the stress-test framing because it is falsifiable: any single uncured test case with the trap in top-10 counts as failure of the claim. Retrieval-utility ceiling. Under exact search (Cell C) HitC@10 ranges from 0.93 to 0.99 across the domains; under the accelerator (Cell D) it is 0.92 to 0.99. On the sealed dedup pools, where the lens-only 3-stage cascade (Cell B, exact scoring) and the accelerator (Cell D) ran on the identical pool  (Table 3)  , the accelerators cost versus the cascades exact scoring is 1.0, 0.3 and 4.0 percentage points of HitC@10 at 5k, 51k and 100k small, growing with pool size (the approximate interior partitioning) while it holds HN@10 = 0.0000 and runs 116143 faster than the cascade on that pool (0.62 vs. 72 at 100k). The open full-pool exact-NN backend (Cell C) was not timed on that pool (6.2). This is operationally useful but not perfect retrieval. The remaining misses are typically in the C-paraphrase differs too much from pattern data-quality issue in the trap corpus that we address with miss-driven curation (documented in the reproducibility repository as the curate_*_paraphrases.py scripts). Retrieval speed as contribution. The 0.61.1 suite retrieval wall-clock at = 100 000 (Cell D, 6.2) is the accelerators contribution: the boundary-conditioned equilibrium solve of 3.9 serves the lens where dense spectral build does not reach the pool at all, andon the same Legal pool116143 faster than the lens-only 3-stage cascade  (Table 3)  . These numbers are measured and SHA-anchored; the accelerators implementation is reserved for commercial use, and an exact-nearest-neighbour substiSmall Learned Projections Reduce Semantic-Reversal Errors in Dense Retrieval tute (Cell C) reproduces every HN@10 number as the open reproducibility path. The safety claim does not depend on the accelerator; the scale-and-latency claim does.

sections.title: 7.3 Limits of the transfer experiment
sections.content: Four domains and twelve mismatched pairs are finite sample. The matrix shows where each lens applies; it does not prove that the recipe cannot fail in another domain. Our best hypothesis for where it might: domains whose traps do not admit clean small edits, or where the A/B/C shape is hard to keep (long-form narrative, multi-paragraph reasoning). The fifth-domain candidates in 9 are chosen partly to probe this. For the Legal Patent cell, 6.4 reports the = 32 follow-up, which lifts that cell above 0.30 while both the = 11 and = 32 lenses keep matched-domain HN@10 = 0.0000.

sections.title: 7.4 Reproducibility protocol summary
sections.content: Any reader with 24 GB of RAM, modern multi-core CPU, and access to 1024dimensional dense encoder can reproduce the claim within working day: 1. Construct 300 matched-shape (A, B, C) triples in the target domain (23 hours of deterministic-script authoring; template provided). 2. Build sentence-split distractor pool from domain corpus (target 50 000 unique 830-word clauses). 3. Embed with E5-Large-v2, no prefix, L2-normalise. 4. Run the preflight duplicate check (preflight_dedup_check.py). Abort if 5 % duplicates. 5. Train the safety lens at = 24 or 32, β = 15 or 17, margin = 0.10, seed = 42 (steering_lens_train.py). Warm-start second round if HN@10 is not yet 0.0000. 6. Measure Cell at pool sizes {5k, 50k, 100k}. Optionally apply the lens to two other domains trap corpora, to see where it applies. Wall-clock: approximately one working day end-to-end on single CPU server.

sections.title: 8 Deployment footprint: small, specialised, hardened indexes
sections.content: A deployed application stores only the lens-projected vectors, not the 1024-D embeddings. For the Legal lens that is = 11 floats per document 44 bytes against 4096, 93 smaller index; the = 32 domains are 32 smaller. Exact nearest-neighbour cost scales with the dimension, so search in the projected space is proportionally cheaper, and at these dimensions an exact scan is realistic again rather than an approximate index. On the cases the lens is declared for, this smaller index is also safer than raw-cosine search over the full embedding (HN@10 = 0.0000 versus 0.811.00); where the raw encoder is weak it is also more accurate (Legal HitC@10 0.99 vs. 0.67). The projected store is application-specific by construction: one declared lens and one index per scope, and the 1024-D embedding cannot be recovered from it. Small Learned Projections Reduce Semantic-Reversal Errors in Dense Retrieval 22 One generalist index 1024-D general-purpose vector database 4096 / vector one shared store HN@10 up to 1.00 (semantic-reversal traps) costly to shard declare + fit one small lens / scope Many specialised indexes (this work) Legal 11-D lens index 44 B/vec Medical 32-D 128 B/vec Contract 11-D 44 B/vec Internal-policy 11-D 44 B/vec ... one declared lens + index per scope HN@10 = 0 on declared 90 smaller cases dimension-proportional search isolatable per tenant Figure 6. Deployment footprint. The lenss output is the stored representation: few floats per document instead of 1024. specialised, semantic-reversal-hardened index per domain or tenant (HN@10 = 0 on its declared cases, 90 smaller, dimension-proportional search) becomes practical alternative to one large general-purpose embedding store. The pattern is enabled by the measured footprint; the comparison is architectural, not benchmark. Implication deployment pattern, not benchmark. Because specialised, semanticreversal-hardened index becomes this small and this cheap to search, running many of them one per domain, tenant, or compliance boundary, each with its own declared lens becomes rational alternative to single large general-purpose vector database (Figure 6): cheaper to store, faster to search, hardened per scope, versionable, and trivially isolatable into separate processes or tenants. It inverts the usual reach for bigger generalist encoder reflex tiny learned projection makes specialisation the cheap option. We state this as the architecture the measured footprint enables; cost or multi-store benchmark is future work. The query-only result (6.7) bounds it: utility holds for the declared cases, not for arbitrary undeclared query phrasings.

sections.title: B Failure modes we documented so nobody repeats them
sections.content: Three implementation errors that reduce the declared-case zero-trap result to noise. Each surfaced in our earlier runs as false negative on the domain-agnostic claim. 1. Reusing lens across domains. lens trained on domain transfers to domain only partly: it lowers HN@10 below raw cosine but does not reach 0.0000 (6.3). For cases, declare and train lens on triples. 2. Shape-mismatched trap triples. If is 15-word question and / are 500word paragraphs, cosine geometry is dominated by length rather than by the adversarial flip. HitC@10 collapses to noise. Match shape. 3. Shape-mismatched distractors. Short-clause A/B/C with paragraph-length distractors produces query-vs-paragraph mismatch that dominates retrieval geometry. Sentence-split the distractor pool to matched clause length. Shape dominates size. In our medical work, 100 matched-shape triples produced HitC@10 = 0.95 while 400 shape-mismatched triples produced HitC@10 = 0.03a 32 spread traceable entirely to shape discipline. This is hard operational lesson and the reason 3.1 leads with the shape invariants.

sections.title: C Hyperparameter sensitivity
sections.content: We report the hyperparameter probes that landed each domains selected lens, so that future replicators can budget training time appropriately. In all cases {24, 32} and margin {0.10, 0.12} worked; only β needed per-domain calibration. Table 8. Per-domain training-loss convergence at each β probe actually run. stable means the training reached Lhinge 0.0001 inside 200 epochs; residual means training completed but with non-zero final loss. This is the only domain where β = 15 was insufficient after warm-start; the cause is that financial-native flips (direction, polarity, period, party) place trap tokens in contexts where E5 embedding proximity is inherently tighter than in the other Small Learned Projections Reduce Semantic-Reversal Errors in Dense Retrieval 27 three domains. Reproducers should budget second warm-start round when the first cold-start β = 15 run leaves residual hn_loss.
